newsitem.title: NORWAY: World jewry to review Holocaust restitution.
newsitem.headline: World jewry to review Holocaust restitution.

text.p: About 150 Jewish leaders meet on Monday to discuss restitution of Jewish property confiscated by the Nazis during the Holocaust in European countries, including Switzerland.

The two-day conference of the World Jewish Congress (WJC), which represents 100 Jewish communities around the world, will also hear evidence of anti-semitism on the Internet computer network, officials said.

They said the opening of the conference would be attended by Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, who will also hold bilateral talks with Jagland and other Norwegian leaders.

The meetings will take place against a backdrop of increasing efforts to search secret Swiss bank records to find out how much money deposited by Jews before and during World War Two was returned to its rightful owners.
"Switzerland during the Second World War acted as the international banking and laundering centre for Nazi Germany," Elan Steinberg, WJC executive director, told a news conference.

A previously secret 1942 U.S. Justice Department document released last week accused Switzerland of being "economically under Axis domination no matter what the sentiments of the people" and said all Swiss imports and exports had to have German or Italian approval.
The document, found in the U.S. National Archive by WJC researchers, also accused Swiss banks of being used by the Nazis to invest German money in the United States and Latin America during the war.

Swiss bankers and politicians, embarrassed by allegations that their country profited from the extermination of six million Jews, are considering whether to create a fund for victims of Nazism in a gesture of reconciliation.

WJC president Edgar Bronfman is expected to give the Jewish leaders at the Oslo meeting a briefing on the success of restitution efforts so far, ask for policy decisions on how to further pursue claims against Swiss banks and discuss whether to expand the campaign to other European countries.

Jewish leaders are praising Norway for its commitment to resolving the issue of restitution. The government last March appointed a committee and gave it one year to map out war-time claims by Jews in Norway, which was occupied by the Nazis in 1940.
Historians say the claims by Norwegian Jews could amount to $80 million but no decision has been taken, Jewish officials said.
WJC Secretary-General Israel Singer said Norway, where half of the 1,500 Jews living in the country before the war were sent to Nazi death camps, was a model of cooperation.

"We are working together with the Norwegian government which called for a solution to this problem. It is something that other countries in western Europe as well as in eastern Europe could learn from. Norway is a model for Europe," Singer said.
"The bad guys are in eastern as well as in western Europe. The only difference is that those in eastern Europe are poorer than those in western Europe. It is not that they are better, or worse."
